report.source_text: The patient underwent 4 chemotherapy cycles consisting of intravenous vincristine 2 mg, doxorubicin 90 mg, endoxan 1400 mg, Dexaven 18 mg, and Zofran 8 mg. Blood parameters were monitored throughout the treatment period. During chemotherapy, gradual tumor regression was observed (Fig. 3A and B), and 1 year after the first cycle of chemotherapy, complete remission was achieved.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 73-year-old man presented with a rapidly progressing skin tumor in the right parotideomasseteric region, initially misdiagnosed as discoid lupus erythematosus. A subsequent biopsy revealed anaplastic large cells in the dermis and subcutaneous tissue, characterized by LCA+, CD30+, ALK-, CD3+ (weak), CD5-, CKAE1/3, MELAN A-, S100-, and Ki67+++, confirming cutaneous anaplastic large-cell lymphoma (C-ALCL). Systemic involvement was ruled out by CT scans of the chest, abdominal cavity, and neck, and a bone marrow trepanobiopsy, which indicated no lymphoma infiltration. The patient underwent 4 cycles of chemotherapy, leading to gradual tumor regression and complete remission after one year.
